story: Every summer, when the ulmo covers the forest in white blossoms and the tineo unfurls its spikes, the hives work to the rhythm of a brief, unrepeatable bloom.
Caramávida lies in the Nahuelbuta range, in the Province of Arauco. A precise territory that shapes the character of every harvest.

science.title: Science & Quality
science.intro: We want the singularity of our honeys to be demonstrated, not just described.
science.bioactivityText: In food science, bioactivity refers to the ability of certain compounds to interact with biological systems. In honey, research typically analyses parameters such as phenolic compound content or antioxidant activity in the laboratory. These values depend on each honey's botanical and geographical origin, which is why we measure them rather than assume them.

rituals.title: How to enjoy it
rituals.intro: A native-forest honey deserves time. A few ideas to discover it.

items.title: With aged cheeses
items.text: A drizzle over cured or blue cheeses balances the salt and lifts the aromas.

items.title: Mountain infusions
items.text: Gently sweetens a herbal infusion without masking its character. Add it once the drink is warm.

items.title: Sourdough bread
items.text: On warm toast, with butter and a pinch of flaky salt.

items.title: Chef’s kitchen
items.text: Glazes, vinaigrettes and desserts that call for a sweetness with identity.

items.title: By the spoonful, slowly
items.text: The purest way to discover its notes: at room temperature, straight from the spoon.
